name: headline_text
label: Headline
default: A site nobody could use with a screen reader, made defensible for procurement

name: problem_richtext
label: The problem
default: An organization was facing procurement and legal accessibility requirements, with a website that simply could not be used with a screen reader. Missing form labels, focus traps in modals, contrast that almost passed, and documents exported without a single tag. The clock was a contract deadline with real money behind it.

name: approach_richtext
label: The approach
default: We ran our three-pass method. First an automated scan to clear the easy wins, knowing tooling catches maybe a third of what is really there. Second a full manual pass: keyboard-only walkthroughs, NVDA and VoiceOver runs, zoom and reflow checks, and PDF tagging with real reading order and honest alt text. Third, the part that matters most, a prioritized remediation report written for the developers who fix it, plus the ACR and VPAT the procurement team actually asked for.

name: result_richtext
label: The result
default: The latest cycle closed and re-tested every critical finding rather than simply logging it. The client walked away with a defensible Accessibility Conformance Report and a site real people can use.
